notes: Summary: Account evaluated Redwood but selected OpenAI/Anthropic direct APIs. Key drivers: perceived simplicity, existing internal SDK experience, immediate credits/discounts from vendor, low procurement friction.
POC outcome: Redwood's hosted API met latency targets (p50 ~90ms for chat, rerank within SLA) and cost estimates were competitive, but internal dev team favored 'same vendor' approach.
Security: Veridian required SSO, KMS integration, and audit logs. Redwood satisfied requirements in demo; procurement stated security was not the blocker.
Quote from Head of Prod: 'We don't want to add another platform during launch — OpenAI gives us predictable SDKs and the brand is already baked into our stack.'
Blocked: no strong executive champion to push a multi-vendor procurement; legal accepted Redwood terms but procurement prioritized speed over negotiation.
Budget: Q1 hiring/hardware freeze reduced appetite for multi-year commitments; preferred pay-as-you-go direct APIs with credits.
Competitive notes: Commercial teams offered a simple integration plan and pre-approved billing for OpenAI; Anthropic appeared in short-list for safety features but lost on existing infra familiarity.
Action items captured: 1) Log win/loss in Sales Ops; 2) Product to review feedback on onboarding friction; 3) Marketing to surface comparison content on 'time-to-launch' case studies.

Internal feedback from SE: POC showed good batching potential and cost parity at scale; recommendation to build clearer migration guides for customers moving from direct APIs to Redwood managed routing.
Next-step for Redwood: conduct a 1:1 product debrief with Sales Ops and pursue a reference ask if Veridian re-evaluates post-launch (unlikely in current Q1 plans).
